prompts.text: Which corner of your hometown would you show a visitor before any of the famous attractions?
The most memorable local guide often knows the quiet places rather than the popular landmarks.
We arrive in the area where you grew up with forty minutes to spare. Where do you take me first?
Walking through streets you knew at school or visiting the places you spend time in now?
Tell me about a shop or street corner you remember for a reason nobody else would guess.
People often describe their old neighbourhoods through details a travel guide would overlook.
Is there a sound or smell which immediately makes a place feel familiar to you?
An ordinary neighbourhood café sometimes tells a better story about a city than its biggest attraction.
I ask for somewhere peaceful near your home, but the usual parks are crowded. Where do we go?
Exploring a small town on foot or taking a slow drive through an unfamiliar city?
Which fictional character would you enjoy having a completely ordinary conversation with?
A good book recommendation comes with a reason rather than an instruction to read it.
We're browsing a bookshop and choose a title for each other using only the covers. How risky is your pick?
A short story which leaves you thinking or a long novel where you miss the characters afterwards?
Tell me about a story somebody told you aloud which stayed with you longer than expected.
The books people abandon sometimes reveal as much about their tastes as the ones they finish.
Do you remember the first book which kept you awake longer than you intended?
Different reading tastes give people more stories to exchange, even when their favourites never overlap.
You find a handwritten note inside a second-hand book. Would you read it or leave it for the next owner?
Reading quietly side by side or listening to someone read a funny passage aloud?
What kind of weather makes you want to go out rather than stay indoors?
A sudden change in weather sometimes improves a day more than following the original plan.
We're halfway through a walk when light rain starts. Do we find shelter or finish the route?
Watching the sunset from somewhere high or taking an early walk while the streets are quiet?
Tell me about a day when the weather changed your plans and left you with a better story.
The same street looks different after rain, especially when everyone moves at a slower pace.
Have you ever travelled somewhere mainly to see its landscape in person?
Enjoying the outdoors doesn't require turning every outing into an exhausting adventure.
I bring a picnic blanket but forget the food. What's the funniest reasonable way to rescue our afternoon?
A garden full of flowers or a waterfront spot where you hear the water moving?
What's the most unexpected place you've seen an animal going about its day?
People's reactions to an overly friendly dog often start surprisingly good conversations.
A curious cat sits beside us at an outdoor café. Who is more likely to make friends with it?
Spending an afternoon around horses or visiting an aquarium to watch sea creatures?
Tell me about an animal encounter which still makes you smile when you remember it.
Some animals behave as though every visitor has arrived specifically to see them.
If you had a garden with space for wildlife, what would you most enjoy seeing there?
You don't need to own a pet to appreciate somebody's endless stories about theirs.
We're walking past a rescue centre with an open day. Would you stop to meet the animals?
Watching playful puppies for an hour or learning how birds recognise their surroundings?
What's your favourite part of a birthday when nobody expects a big celebration?
Remembering why a date matters to someone feels more thoughtful than making a fuss about it.
A friend invites us to a small celebration with no dress code. What would you wear to feel comfortable?
A surprise cake with a few close people or a relaxed meal where everyone knows the plan?
Tell me about a celebration where something small went wrong and became everyone's favourite memory.
The best part of some parties happens in the kitchen while everyone else looks for the music.
Are you more likely to keep birthday cards or the photographs people take on the day?
A celebration doesn't have to be loud to feel worth remembering.
We're helping set up a friend's party, but the decorations arrive late. Which task would you volunteer to handle?
Making a homemade gift for someone or taking them to choose something they genuinely want?
